chunks: And if We had revealed it to some of the non-Arabs

key_terms.الْأَعْجَمِينَ: The non-Arabs / foreigners (those who do not speak Arabic)

ai.seo_question: Why was the Quran revealed in Arabic and not to a non-Arab?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the divine wisdom in selecting a native Arab speaker to ensure the Quran's linguistic miracle was accessible and undeniable to its primary audience, thereby removing the pretext of linguistic alienation. It highlights that the rejection by the Quraysh was not due to the message's content or the Prophet's foreignness, but their deliberate refusal to accept truth despite its clarity in their own tongue. This context reinforces the concept of 'I'jaz' (inimitability) as a tangible, linguistic proof rather than a mystical abstraction.
